prose.text: The chunk's own probes come first, then the two live legs, then the standard gate set in test-plan §3 order: `capability-drift` before the default-features workspace nextest, the `--features mcp-server` bindings regen as the last cargo-adjacent step, and the base-identity bindings close, since the chunk adds no procedure. The operator pass follows.

The two live legs boot the release app on this host under a virtual display. Each moves the receivers to 14317 and 14318 through the two port variables, so the shared ports 4317 and 4318 are never bound; each unsets `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` so the window opens on the virtual display; each writes a fresh data dir under `target/`. The `boot` verb rebuilds the release binary itself, so the legs read the tree as it stands. A reading taken under heavy host load says so in the evidence.

Absences, each with its reason: - No webview gate and no headful self-verify: no `pulse-app/ui/**` path is touched. - No local pre-push gate: `cargo xtask pre-push:linux` cannot run on this host (test-plan amendment   `2026-10-02-incident-events-readable-through-mcp`); CI is the gate the push meets. - No bus-stopped leg in the fence: it needs a private bus daemon and a config file that is not in the tree. The   `session_bus` label is pinned at unit level against a real Unix listener; research ran the live control once. - No Windows leg: nothing runs `scripts/agent-run.ps1` here or in CI. - No targeted nextest entry: step 1 runs the two test targets as the red-before-green pair; the workspace entry   runs the same tests on every re-run.

On the untouched tree both live legs read red: `harness:settled` does not exist yet. The control leg's exit code is not what decides it, since `xvfb-run` itself returns non-zero when its display server is already gone; its `contains` atoms decide it.

**The operator pass, in this order.** 1. The hygiene entry, then the pre-CI commit, then the build-branch push. 2. The CI read of the pushed tip, whole, **report-only**. This run is the first in which the smoke reads the app    past its windows' settle on a runner, and it may end either way. It is recorded as it ends and never re-run. 3. Three report-only reads of that run by its id, as `<id>`: the jobs listing; the boot job's log lines that carry    the settle verdict, the readiness line and the cleanup token; the run's `logs-boot-Linux` artifact, downloaded    under `target/`, with `harness-settled.json` and `xvfb.log` printed. 4. **The stop.** If the settle verdict of that run reads `ended` or `not-settled`, the pass stops and says what the    job kept: the exit record, `app_exit_record`, `display`, `session_bus`, and what `xvfb.log` holds. Naming the    cause from it and closing it are the operator's next word; nothing is fixed on top without it. If it reads    `settled`, the run is green reading 1 of the count to eleven and the chunk goes to the wrap.
Evidence files are written by /implement and by the operator pass from the entries' recorded outputs; no entry writes one.
